description:
The Ruxox Farm site represents an extensive area of continuous human occupation from the Late Iron Age through to the early 5th century CE. Archaeological evidence reveals a complex settlement featuring a wide array of Roman artefacts, including high quantities of local and imported pottery, roof tiles, metalworking debris such as crucibles, and a cemetery containing over 30 inhumations as well as cremations. While the height of the settlement's prosperity appears to have occurred in the mid-2nd century, the broader site spans roughly 50 acres and includes traces of undisturbed sandstone foundations, plaster floors, and a possible bridge or jetty.

Scholars suggest a temple may have existed at Ruxox Farm due to a remarkable concentration of ritualistic finds and distinctive architectural cropmarks. Compelling evidence includes the recovery of at least 72 pipeclay figurines, potentially the largest collection from a rural site in Britain, primarily depicting the goddess Venus and _Dea Nutrix_ (Nursing Goddess). These mass-produced icons suggest a sacred focal point for healing or fertility rites, especially given that pipeclay figurines of *Dea Nutrix* have previously been associated with the burials of children. Furthermore, aerial photography has identified a possible rectangular enclosure within a larger prehistoric oval enclosure east of the farm, which would align well with layout of a Romano-British temple _temenos_.
